title: Cardboard-Box Construction
strapline: A big empty box is a rocket, a den, a bus — the best toy is often the packaging.
intent: Children design and build big structures from boxes, planning, problem-solving and seeing an idea take shape.
Children join, cut, tape and balance, developing practical construction skills and hand strength.
Children turn boxes into settings for imaginative play — a car, a castle, a rocket — merging making and role-play.
Children work at a big, satisfying scale, using their whole bodies and often working together.
Children experience the whole creative arc: an idea, a plan, the making, the setbacks, the finished thing.
implementation: Gather boxes of all sizes and keep a stock, plus joining materials — tape, split pins, string, treasury tags.
Start from the children's ideas: 'what shall we make?' and let a plan emerge, sketching it if it helps.
Offer safe cutting tools and teach their use — child scissors, and adult-supervised cutting of thick card.
Model problem-solving aloud when a join fails: 'the roof keeps falling — what could hold it up?'
Let structures be big — a box car to sit in, a rocket to stand in — and give the space and time they need.
Add paint, decorating materials and role-play props once the structure is built, so play continues.
Keep works-in-progress up across days so children can return, refine and extend their builds.
key_questions: What are you going to make? What will it need?
How could you join these two boxes together?
The roof keeps falling — what could we try?
How can you make a door that really opens?
What could you add to make it even better?

impact.text: Children plan and build a structure from an idea.
Children join, cut and balance materials with growing skill.
Children solve construction problems and adapt when things fail.
Children use their building for imaginative, role-play purposes.
Children work together on a big, shared build.
Children see a project through and take pride in it.

enhancements: A stock of boxes in graded sizes, plus tubes and packaging.
A joining trolley — tape, split pins, string, treasury tags, hole punch.
Paint and decorating materials for once the build is done.
Role-play props to match likely builds — steering wheel, telephone, crown.
A design corner with paper and pens to sketch plans first.
A challenge card: build something big enough to sit inside.

playing_exploring: Children explore what boxes can become and how they join.
They test and combine boxes to see what holds and stands.
active_learning: Children stay with a big build across days, refining it.
They keep trying when a join or a roof won't hold.
creating_thinking: Children design a structure and plan how to make it.
They solve problems and adapt their build as they go.
